meta.disclaimer: Educational clinical reference only — not a prescription and not a substitute for professional judgement. Verify every dose against the current primary source and local formulary before prescribing. Definitive dental treatment is the priority; analgesics are for temporary relief.
meta.notes: US analgesia figures extracted from the ADA 2024 (adults/adolescents) and ADA 2023 (children) guidelines plus AAPD 'Useful Medications' for paediatric weight-based dosing and the FDA 2017 codeine/tramadol restriction. UK adult figures reflect SDCEP guidance and BNF maxima. UK paediatric doses are pending extraction from BNFc. All 'verified' rules still require DDS sign-off before release.

recommendation.summary: NSAID alone, or NSAID combined with acetaminophen, is first-line; it likely gives superior pain relief with a better safety profile than opioids.

components.notes: Take with food; use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

options.label: Ibuprofen + acetaminophen (combination)
options.notes: Combination NSAID + acetaminophen is generally more effective than either alone; keep each drug within its daily maximum.

components.notes: Lower daily ceiling in hepatic impairment / chronic alcohol use.

rules.rationale: The ADA panel found a beneficial net balance favouring non-opioid medications; NSAIDs alone or with acetaminophen likely provide superior pain relief with a more favourable safety profile than opioids.
rules.source_locator: Pharmacologic management recommendations; first-line non-opioid therapy.

recommendation.summary: Reserve opioids for when first-line non-opioids are insufficient or contraindicated; use the lowest dose for the shortest duration (typically no more than 3 days).

components.notes: Avoid routine 'just-in-case' prescribing. Exert extreme caution in adolescents and young adults. Consider combining with a non-opioid rather than escalating opioid dose.

rules.rationale: Opioids should be reserved for clinical situations where first-line therapy is insufficient or NSAIDs are contraindicated; routine just-in-case opioid prescribing should be avoided.
rules.source_locator: Recommendations on opioid use and good practice statements.

recommendation.summary: NSAIDs (ibuprofen) alone or with acetaminophen are recommended first-line for acute dental pain in children; opioids are not first-line.

components.notes: Per AAPD Useful Medications; do not exceed adult ceiling.
Hepatotoxic in overdose; count all acetaminophen-containing products.

options.label: Alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen (moderate–severe)
options.notes: For moderate–severe pain, staggering the two agents can improve control; keep each within its own limits.

rules.rationale: The ADA children's panel found a small beneficial net balance favouring NSAIDs alone or with acetaminophen versus no analgesic therapy for acute dental pain.
rules.source_locator: Recommendations for NSAIDs +/- acetaminophen in children; AAPD dosing table.

recommendation.summary: Do not use codeine or tramadol in children < 12; do not use tramadol < 18 after tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy; avoid both in adolescents 12–18 with obesity, obstructive sleep apnoea, or severe lung disease.

contraindications: tramadol < 18 years after tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy
codeine/tramadol in 12–18 y with obesity, OSA, or severe lung disease (increased respiratory-depression risk)
cautions: ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolisers at risk of life-threatening respiratory depression
rules.rationale: The FDA contraindicates codeine and tramadol in young children due to the risk of serious, life-threatening breathing problems; the ADA children's guideline aligns with avoiding these agents.

recommendation.summary: In adolescents (12–17), NSAID ± acetaminophen remains first-line. Do NOT use tramadol after tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy (contraindicated < 18 y), and avoid codeine/tramadol in those with obesity, obstructive sleep apnoea, or severe lung disease.

contraindications: codeine/tramadol in 12–18 y with obesity, OSA, or severe lung disease
cautions: ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolisers are at risk of respiratory depression
rules.rationale: The FDA restricts codeine and tramadol in adolescents at risk of respiratory depression; non-opioids are first-line.

recommendation.summary: Manage acute dental pain with analgesics (ibuprofen and/or paracetamol), not antibiotics; antibiotics do not treat pain.

components.frequency: three times daily (with or after food)

options.label: Ibuprofen + paracetamol
options.notes: The two may be combined/alternated for better relief.

rules.rationale: SDCEP advises that dental pain is managed with analgesics and appropriate dental treatment; antibiotics are not indicated for pain relief. Doses follow BNF.
rules.source_locator: SDCEP Drug Prescribing for Dentistry — analgesics / management of dental pain; BNF ibuprofen & paracetamol.

recommendation.summary: Ibuprofen and/or paracetamol at BNFc weight/age-based doses; antibiotics do not relieve pain.

components.max_daily: up to 40 mg/kg/day (max 1200 mg without specialist advice)
components.notes: Not for infants under 3 months / under 5 kg; give with or after food.

components.frequency: every 4–6 h as needed (max 4 doses in 24 h)
components.notes: BNFc age bands as a proxy for weight; do not exceed 4 doses in 24 h.

rules.rationale: SDCEP/BNFc: manage paediatric dental pain with analgesics at age/weight-appropriate doses.
